What would be the right way here ?

Please use '-f' and create a separate commit. I'll take it from there and import the change to
samba's version of pidl.

Except `dom_sid28 and SID` types, all other types have single line code handler. I am not sure whether other uses of dom_sid28/SID will work with current tab counts in this commit. 

I will add it as separate commit.

I guess we want to change dissect_ndr_nt_SID28() to take @HF@ as explicit last argument as all others.

While looking at it dissect_ndr_nt_SID_with_options() seems to be completely unused
Ya. I didn't want to remove it. Can you please review the latest changes ?

It seems that you have rewritten the whole idl file, because all tabs are changed to whitespaces.

Please reformat it, so that it's possible to see the changes and that we can port the changes to
Samba, as the idl file should be exactly the same.

Thanks!

In my experience working with pidl related stuff in wireshark, i was not able to use the samba idl without much modification on the wireshark side.

In this case, i took the samba IDL and fixed all the errors in the codegen process.
Lot of DRSUAPI structures includes linked pointers. I remember it failed when i left it as it is on the wireshark side.

Ok, I just noticed that wireshark upstream don't use pidl for drsuapi.idl yet.

So your approach is basically correct!

But please use the same indentation in the idl file as the samba idl file,
so that's possible to add further syncs without much work and tricks
like using 'git diff -w' in order to see the real changes.

I've converted wireshark to use pidl instead here:
https://git.samba.org/?p=metze/wireshark/wip.git;a=history;f=epan/dissectors/pidl/drsuapi;hb=refs/heads/ws-metze-current

That very much work in progress as it requires quite some hacks, but
it allows me to learn kerberos keys on the fly from the replication
traffic in order to decrypt other following packets in a capture file.
Which is very useful to debug samba kerberos tests against a windows
server, which create temporary accounts, replicate them temporary,
use them and delete them again.

Thanks look much better now!

Ok, now I see it was now generated by pidl, but what command did you use?

The idl files under epan/dissectors/dcerpc/ are the ones for idl2wrs instead of pidl if
I understand the situation correct.

I typically use 'pushd epan/dissectors/pidl/ && make ;popd' in order to regenerate the
dissectors using pidl. I added the same idl files under epan/dissectors/pidl/drsuapi,
see https://git.samba.org/?p=metze/wireshark/wip.git;a=commitdiff;h=7beadd12d486d8f0a4297aaabb8df3ed9c1942c1. Maybe you want to use 'git mv epan/dissectors/dcerpc/drsuapi epan/dissectors/pidl/drsuapi' and take the CMakeLists.txt changes from my commit?

I don't think wireshark build system autogenerate and checkin those files automatically. I usually generate those files manually checkin the generated files.

`~/wireshark/tools/pidl/pidl --outputdir ~/outdir/ --ws-parser -- svcctl.idl`

I didn't knew about `idl2wrs`. 

Sure i will move it.

Thanks! Can you please adjust the indentation for drsuapi_ReadNgcKey to use tabs instead of
whitespaces in order to match the rest of the file?
Thanks!
